MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JUNE 5, 2023

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:05 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES FOR THE MEETING OF MAY 1,
  2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
to,
  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

B.  2023 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JANUARY 1, 2023 THROUGH MAY
  31, 2023.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 6B

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230160; ADDRESS: 17 HIDDEN VALLEY, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: AUGUSTO J. CACERES; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-230161) for a 613 square-foot first story
  addition, 623 square-foot second-story addition, and the construction of a second-floor
  balcony to an existing two-story single-family residence.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  1
 Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. He added that the
applicant submitted revised renderings to staff after the agenda was posted and they were
distributed to the Planning Commission prior to the meeting; copies were available for the
members of the public in attendance. The revision is the use of a standing metal seam roof as
opposed to the originally proposed asphalt shingle roof; there were no other significant changes.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-230160 (NC-230161) with the conditions outlined in the staff report.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that the staff report notes that the balcony was proposed
at 362 sq. ft. and was reduced to 229 sq. ft. to ensure that the easterly neighbors’ privacy would
be maintained. He asked what the reason was for the applicant to make this change.

Riad Itani, PE, Designer, stated that he and the property owner, Mr. Caceres, spoke to the
neighbors about the project. The neighbor to the east of the property had a concern with privacy
due to the view from the proposed balcony and their pool. To resolve this issue, the property
owner agreed to push back the balcony and reduce the size of the balcony; the property owner
has also agreed to add landscaping to further help with privacy.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE PA-230160, A REQUEST FOR A NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY
  DETERMINATION (NC-230161) FOR A 613 SQUARE-FOOT FIRST STORY ADDITION,
  623 SQUARE-FOOT SECOND-STORY ADDITION, AND THE CONSTRUCTION OF A
  SECOND-FLOOR BALCONY TO AN EXISTING TWO-STORY SINGLE-FAMILY
  RESIDENCE PURSUANT TO THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT
  AND THE ADDITIONAL CONDITION TO ADD LANDSCAPING TO ADDRESS THE
  EASTERLY NEIGHBORS’ PRIVACY CONCERN.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-230160 for 17 Hidden Valley Road, there is a 20-day appeal period whereby any member of
the public or the City Council may appeal the project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230152; ADDRESS: 25915 CHALMETTE LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES CA 90274; APPLICANT: JOHN WHITCOMBE; A request for
  a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-230153) for on-site improvements
  including the installation of retaining walls, grading, and the installation of a sports court
  at the rear of the property. Minor Deviation (MD-230154) for exceeding the maximum
  allowable lot coverage by no more than 10%. Grading application (G-230155) for grading
  on a slope greater than 35% (average slope ratio is 2:1) relating to the installation of
  retaining walls and sports court.

Commissioner Olson recused himself because he lives within 500’ of the subject property and
Commissioner Schachter recused himself due to a personal relationship with the applicants. Both
Commissioners recused themselves at 7:18 p.m.

Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. The applicant has
been approved for several permits throughout the past year on a ministerial level. It was after
approval of Planning Application OC-220434 that staff issued a “stop work” order for excessive
grading and retaining walls that were done on the property, which was outside of the scope of the
original permit. Staff advised the applicant that Planning Commission review would be required
for the work. Associate Planner Flores noted an error in the staff report on page 2, where it states
that this property does not have an HOA; it is actually under the Masongate HOA; however, HOA
approval is not required for this type of work.

Correspondence was received after the agenda was distributed and was provided to the Planning
Commission prior to the meeting; copies were available for the members of the public in
attendance.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-230152, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-230153) for after-the-fact approval
of unpermitted on-site improvements including the installation of retaining walls, grading, and the
installation of a sports court at the rear of the property. A Minor Deviation (MD-230154) to exceed
the maximum allowable lot coverage by no more than 10% and a Grading Application (G-230155)
for grading on a slope greater than 35% relating to the installation of retaining walls and a sports
court subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  2
 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about permits for the retaining wall. Associate Planner
Flores stated that at this time there is no permit for the retaining wall. If this project is approved,
the applicant will be required to submit plans to the Building Department for plan check. The
inspector will review the plans and ensure that they are consistent with what was done on the
site.

Shane Lamb, Extreme Hillsides, stated that he is representing John Whitcomb and is present in
lieu of Keith Tucker, Engineer. He stated that Keith Tucker has reviewed the job and done boring
samples; his next step will be to do a soils report. Some of the walls that have been constructed
are under three feet and some exceed three feet; the property owner is willing to lower the backfill
levels to avoid having to engineer the walls. He stated that the retaining wall is a spread footing
deeper than the top fills and does not have a clear idea how deep the bedrock is.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Mr. Lamb confirmed that a soils
report has not been done but the borings have been taken.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Director Naughton stated that Building and Safety will
require a full grading plan, drainage plan, and soils report in order to return with a recommendation
on what will need to be done.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Associate Planner Flores stated that
the work is complete; however, the sports court was removed. Mr. Lamb confirmed that the sports
court was removed; it was a synthetic sports court that snaps together and was not difficult to
remove.

Doug Whitcomb, Property Owner, stated that he has done many projects in the city and this is
the first time there has been issues with one of his projects. Mr. Whitcomb stated that he was
gone for about a month; his project supervisors, head of landscape, and main supervisor spoke
with Associate Planner Flores. After their conversation, they understood that they were allowed
to build planter walls on the hillside so long as they did not exceed three feet. Mr. Whitcomb stated
that there have been numerous complaints from the neighbors and issues from the beginning. He
stated that this is going to be an orchard with fruit trees and the walls were not intended to retain
nor were they necessary. He stated that there was a flat area originally and unfortunately the
photographs showing the site prior to the work, which were provided to staff, were not presented.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked why the neighbors are upset. Mr. Whitcomb stated a survey
was done and it was discovered that one of his neighbors had taken approximately a 20’x 60’
portion of his property from the previous owner who has passed away.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked Mr. Whitcomb if he had received authorization from city
staff and city engineering to build the retaining walls without a permit. Mr. Whitcomb stated that it
was a verbal approval and his project supervisors and head of landscape were under the
impression that three foot walls were okay. Mr. Whitcomb stated that many inspectors have been
to his property and stated that the current inspector found that the work could not be approved.

Darrin Stovall, 4616 Sugarhill Drive, asked why the appropriate permits were not obtained
beforehand. Mr. Whitcomb stated that he was of the understanding that a three-foot planter wall
would not require a permit. He stated that after so many complaints he submitted the plans to
Associate Planner Flores and they were approved and stamped and there was a stipulation about
the amount of dirt that could be removed; he also stated that he has never done work on a hill.

Mr. Stovall stated that his property abuts the subject property where the dirt was removed; he
wants to be sure that the work was done properly. He added that he had proposed to add square
footage to his home; however, he could not do so due to being over the maximum allowable lot
coverage. He stated that he does not have any objection to the project and expressed his concern
that they are obtaining permits after-the-fact.

Salvador Aguilar, 25914 Chalmette Lane, stated that he built a brand-new home and went through
the Planning Approval process. He stated that he is a General Contractor and knows the rules
and stated that everyone abides by the same rules. He stated that he does not have an issue with
the project; however, he should be required do things the right way.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that one correspondence noted concern with the bridle
trail that runs along the rear of the property. Director Naughton stated that during plan check, the
grading and drainage plans will be reviewed for any off-site impacts.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  APPROVE PA-230152, A NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION (NC-
  230153) FOR AFTER-THE-FACT APPROVAL OF UNPERMITTED ON-SITE

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  3
   IMPROVEMENTS INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF RETAINING WALLS,
  GRADING, AND THE INSTALLATION OF A SPORTS COURT AT THE REAR OF THE
  PROPERTY. A MINOR DEVIATION (MD-230154) TO EXCEED THE MAXIMUM
  ALLOWABLE LOT COVERAGE BY NO MORE THAN 10% AND A GRADING
  APPLICATION (G-230155) FOR GRADING ON A SLOPE GREATER THAN 35%
  RELATING TO THE INSTALLATION OF RETAINING WALLS AND A SPORTS COURT
  SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT PURSUANT TO
  THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL
  CONDITIONS TO REQUIRE AN ENGINEERING REPORT, SOILS REPORT, AND THAT
  STAFF WILL MONITOR THIS PROJECT.

AYES: Yoo, Romanelli, Nicklas
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar
RECUSE: Olson, Schachter

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-230152 for 25915 Chalmette Lane, there is a 20-day appeal period whereby any member of
the public or the City Council may appeal the project.

Commissioner Schachter and Commissioner Olson returned to join the meeting at 7:56 p.m.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

Community Development Director Naughton provided a presentation with a summary of the staff
report. Staff is seeking direction on land uses in the Commercial District that will be permitted “by-
right”; conditionally permitted (requiring a Conditional Use Permit); or prohibited.

Director Naughton posed the following questions for discussion:

  •  Should Restaurants/Delicatessens be permitted or conditionally permitted?
  •  Distinction between whether a restaurant includes odor-producing activities such as a
  smoker or charbroiler? Should there be locational standards, if so?
  •  Should a CUP be required for restaurants that serve alcohol?

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is inclined to keep as much discretion as possible.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER OLSON, Director Naughton stated that when a
case is reviewed, staff looks at it from all angles (a new business owner, resident, and staff); staff
would like direction on the need to require a CUP for certain land use or if there is good reason
to require a discretionary review.

COMMISSIONER SCACHTER stated that the city typically processes applications quickly and
maintains that the city should keep as much discretion as possible.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed and added that this will be especially helpful with the city
moving toward more mixed-use developments.

COMMISSIONER’S NICKLAS AND OLSON also agreed with requiring CUPs for restaurants and
delicatessens.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Director Naughton stated that there have been a few
restaurant openings in the past year at Peninsula Center; however, they have a Master CUP for
certain buildings. The CUP process typically takes about 2-3 months. The total timeframe with
permits could take about 6 months.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that if a
business occupying the space has not been out of business for more than 6 months, a similar
business could utilize the space under the same CUP.

  •  Should medical offices be permitted or conditionally permitted?
  •  Should there be expanded definition that distinguish office use v clinic or in-patient,
  surgical, etc. and related CUP requirements?

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if there are more medical uses at the Promenade. Director
Naughton stated that The Promenade has a Master CUP for medical office use; however, they
are limited to a certain percentage.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  4
 COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated since there is going to be more mixed-use, then the city
should have oversight.

CHAIR YOO AND COMMISSIONER NICKLAS agreed.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that she
does not believe that the Peninsula Center includes medical office uses in their Master CUP; the
medical offices that are currently at the Peninsula Center have a separate CUP.

There was a consensus among the Planning Commissioners to require a CUP for medical office
uses.

  •  Should Learning/Tutorial Centers be permitted or conditionally permitted?
  •  Department policy has been to allow these uses without a CUP as long as they are
  smaller-scale operations, that includes one-on-one sessions and groups of <15 students.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that there are concerns about traffic controls in the areas
where learning/tutorial centers come in; for this reason, a CUP should be required.

CHAIR YOO asked about the size limitation and putting restrictions on small business owners
with very little foot traffic and asked why this would be different than a professional office. Director
Naughton stated that smaller learning/tutorial centers with less than 1,000 sq. ft. would not
function different than a general professional office; however, the larger centers with 25 or more
students will cause more of a traffic/parking impact.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if there is a threshold where the CUP process would become
onerous for a small business owner. Director Naughton stated that a CUP application is a
minimum of $2,000; they also need to hire someone to draw up plans; and the cost of any tenant
improvements. Director Naughton stated that the Planning Fees have not been updated in years
and there will be a fee study and the fees will be going up.

A brief discussion ensued on the threshold to require a CUP.

Director Naughton stated that she will do research on occupancy and tenant spaces sizes and
return to the Planning Commission with this information.

Director Naughton stated that there are conflicting provisions in between the CG and the CL with
food/groceries/markets. In the CG it is conditionally permitted and in the CL it is permitted by-
right.

  •  Should food/groceries/markets be permitted or conditionally permitted in CG/CDMU?
  •  Should there be a distinction between size of tenant space in determining CUP or by-right
  determination?
  •  Should seating area for in-store market dining be permitted as ancillary use or
  conditionally permitted?

A brief discussion ensued about the size of the tenant spaces.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that there
have not been any conflicts due to the conflicting provisions; however, if an application were
submitted a CUP would be required.

Director Naughton stated that she will look into the tenant space sizes and bring this back to the
Planning Commission.

CHAIR YOO commented that in-store dining could be similar to restaurant use.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that both should be categorized the same.

Director Naughton stated that there is another conflict in CG and CL with laundromats.

  •  Should laundromats be conditionally permitted in CG/CDMU?

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that although
there are no existing laundromats in the city; it should be considered that there is an increase in
residential units in the commercial district and they may not all have their own laundry facilities.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER OLSON, Director Naughton stated that if there
was a proposal for laundry facilities that are open to the public in a mixed-use development, then

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  5
 it would be considered a laundromat.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that this is a use that should require discretionary review
due to the traffic and noise.

CHAIR YOO stated that if a laundromat was proposed then the residents may have a need for it
and would not want to put restrictions on a use that is needed.

A discussion ensued on the need for this use.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that due to the hours and possible parking issues, he
considers that a CUP should still be required.

In response to a question by CHAIR YOO, Director Naughton stated that laundry facilities are not
required by code in multi-family developments, but they can be. She added that typically multi-
family developments for sale include laundry hook-ups or common laundry facilities as an
amenity.

  •  Should drive-in or drive-through food facilities continue to be prohibited or should they be
  conditionally permitted uses?

A brief discussion ensued.

There was consensus among the commissioners to continue to prohibit this use.

  •  Should amusement arcades continue to be prohibited or should they be conditionally
  permitted uses?

CHAIR YOO asked about the drawback to having an arcade on the hill. Director Naughton stated
that the property owners who most recently were proposing an arcade wanted to provide
additional activites for kids, other than going to the movies or restaurants; she is not sure what
the drawback was in the past.

A brief discussion ensued.

There was a consensus among the commissioners to conditionally permit amusement arcades.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

The Planning Commission tentatively agreed to hold a Special Planning Commission meeting on
July 10. Director Naughton stated that if the Special Planning Commission meeting date is
confirmed, the July 3 meeting will be canceled, and the required Notice of Cancellation will be
posted.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked about the corner of PVDN and PVDE; Director Naughton
stated that the MWD work has been completed; the corner will be developed as a pocket park.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton provided the schedule and map for Waste Management’s service changes.

Director Naughton provided information on Planning Commissioner training which is being offered
by The Institute for Local Government on Friday, June 23.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - APRIL 25, 2023

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - MAY 9, 2023

C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - MAY 23, 2023

D.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION - MAY 30, 2023 (BUDGET STUDY SESSION)

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
to,

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023
  6
 11.  ADJOURNMENT IN MEMORY OF JOAN FRIEDMAN, CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PLANNING COMMISSIONER

At 9:08 p.m., CHAIR YOO adjourned the Planning Commission meeting in memory of Planning
Commissioner and Rolling Hills Estates resident, Joan Friedman. The City of Rolling Hills Estates
extends its deepest condolences to Joan Friedman’s family, friends, and community.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on Monday, July 3, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.in the
City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Victor Yoo, Chair

  7
